caption:
The front catches your eye. The back gives you the details. 🔎

“Natural,” “multigrain,” and “no added sugar” each tell you only part of the story. Check the ingredients and nutrition information, compare similar foods using the same amount, then consider your actual portion.

Save this for your next grocery shop.

Fictional packs and illustrative numbers. AI-generated imagery and narration.

Sources:
FDA: https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-food-labeling-and-critical-foods/use-term-natural-food-labeling
NDSU Extension: https://www.ndsu.edu/agriculture/sites/default/files/2022-03/fn726.pdf
American Heart Association: https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/eat-smart/sugar/difference-between-sugar-free-and-no-added-sugar
FDA label guide: https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-facts-label/how-understand-and-use-nutrition-facts-label
